subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Sharp pain on the right side of the abdomen, just below the ribs, which radiates to the lower abdomen and groin.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: Hi, I'm Russell. I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm a male. I've been having this sharp pain on the right side of my abdomen, just below my ribs, for the last several days. It feels like it goes down to my lower abdomen and into my groin, and it comes and goes, but when it does, it's really bad. I can't find a comfortable position when it's happening. Doctor: Could you please provide your approximate age and confirm if you have experienced any associated symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, fever, or changes in your urinary habits (e.g., frequency, urgency, blood in urine)? Patient: I'm not sure about my exact age, but I'm a male. I have felt nauseated, though I haven't vomited. The pain is accompanied by a burning sensation when I urinate, and sometimes my urine looks a little dark, though I don't think there's any frank blood. Doctor: Have you had any prior episodes of similar pain, and have you been diagnosed with kidney stones, urinary tract infections, or gallstones in the past? Patient: Yes, I've had kidney stones before, but I've been able to pass them. This one is taking a lot longer, though. Doctor: Have you experienced any fever, chills, or changes in urinary frequency or volume associated with the pain? Patient: I haven't had a fever or chills, and I don't notice any significant changes in how often I urinate, just that it burns a little when I do. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as a CT scan or ultrasound, for this current episode of pain? If so, what were the findings? Patient: I saw my doctor, and they ordered a CT scan, which showed a kidney stone in the right ureter. They sent me to see a urologist after that. Doctor
